title: Normalized square existence for a uniformizer quotient
statement: For prime l, finite intermediate E, a maximal-ideal uniformizer pi, n, a morphism f:X -> S, and an integral full universal right-derived model R, the actual quotient map O_E -> O_E/(pi)^(n+1) admits a full-unit-normalized RestrictionSquare between R and the canonical quotient right-derived model.

proof.text: Use transparent aliases for the original derived model and normalized square, to share category instances. Apply the resolution-free existence component of the finite-free scalar-squares theorem (normalized scalar pullback data, conjugate restriction/direct-image isomorphism with the full cochain-unit equation, transport to R by rightDerivedUnique) to the actual quotient map and the supplied integral right-derived model R.

mathlib_searches.results: Existing declarations provide the finite perfect-model and universal-unit APIs, but no concrete quotient square theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No direct existing theorem; split the two missing components.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_uniformizer_restriction_square
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers l E)) (n : ℕ)
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (R : ScalarRightDerived (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) f) :
    Nonempty (CanonicalScalarSquare (quotientMap l E π n) f R)
lean.note: Transparent ScalarRightDerived, CanonicalScalarSquare, and ScalarMateIsIso aliases preserve the expanded statement definitionally while sharing its category instances.
